To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) We present a method based on transfer and multi-task learning for predicting protein protein interactions (PPi), in the absence of labeled data.
we have shown how transfer learning can be used to predict protein interactions in a target task with no known interactions available, by utilizing the labeled interactions from other species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of predicting protein interactions between host and pathogens, where there is a paucity of data available for the host-pathogen interaction of interest.
the problem of building predictive models in the context of host-pathogen protein protein interactions, when labeled examples are not available.
the development of a transfer learning method for host-pathogen PPIs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is able to predict host-pathogen interactions with a higher accuracy than other methods, when the source and target data are related.
transfer learning is indeed useful in predicting interactions in a task with no known interactions available, and the right choice of the source examples is crucial in achieving this.
our proposed method outperforms the baseline method on the target task, when we use the right source examples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method is able to achieve a 0.8% increase in the area under ROC curve (AUC) when compared to the baseline method, when there are 10 labeled examples in the target task.
we show that it is possible to build a predictive model for a task, where there are no labeled examples.

we have proposed a method to predict protein protein interactions in unlabeled data, which utilizes labeled data from other related tasks, and that the choice of the right examples from the source tasks makes a significant difference.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when there is no labeled data for a task, one should use labeled data from related tasks to train a predictive model.
, transfer learning can be applied in the absence of labeled data in the target task.
the performance of a predictive model on an unlabeled task can be improved by choosing the right examples from the source tasks.
